review_summary: The F1849 framework is built and verified, both generated meshes and all six images are verified and genuine, and the handoff/report are honest about the partial result. The verdict is INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE because the donor ODBs for the two generated cases are NOT in the repo (404 at both the handoff checkpoint 92815645 and the latest commit 03360b80), so the mesh-to-donor causal chain is REPORTED_ONLY, not independently verifiable — the same defect class as F1838 and F1846. Cases 1 and 3 are BLOCKED on missing donors, so the four-case reproduction is incomplete (2 of 4). The Case 2 count parity (17,280) is from a 'Calibrated Advancing Crack Envelope v2' whose prior calibration is not reconstructed, so count parity is not scientific acceptance. The handoff also corrects the F1849 premise: F1779 Cases 3 and 5 used stress-error donors, not the damage envelope, so all-damage sizing for Cases 3/5 is a different experiment from F1779, not a reproduction. The Case 5 negative result (4,375 el, -71.46%) is real and informative: the damage envelope fails on an elastic donor with no evolving damage.

gaps.detail: Case 2 donor models/pandey_kumar_mode1/224_f1734_case2_distal_refinement/PK_F1779_CASE2_ENVELOPE.odb (claimed 518,260,408 B, SHA 0aa9601559f26859d6a8b5e814153dbac27d4a6a4cb932a2f9c0457b4c8d58d8) returns 404 via GitHub API get_file_contents and raw HEAD at BOTH the handoff checkpoint 92815645 and the latest commit 03360b80; the API directory listing of 224_f1734_case2_distal_refinement does not list it. Case 5 donor models/pandey_kumar_mode1/218_f1726_seven_hole_study/PK_F1726_SEVEN_HOLE_COARSE.odb (claimed 194,344,892 B, SHA cb673713fde31593ae452a21bc05bffc140bccce71f1d43d601ee17b43802b0e) also returns 404 at both commits. Both donor SHAs are therefore REPORTED_ONLY (local files), and the mesh-to-donor causal chain is not independently verifiable from the repo. Same defect class as F1838 and F1846. gaps.title: Case 2 count parity is from a 'calibrated envelope v2', not a reconstructed F1779 calibration
gaps.detail: The report and handoff state the Case 2 envelope is frame ID 9999, description 'Calibrated Advancing Crack Envelope v2', and 'its prior calibration is not reconstructed or relabeled as unmodified F1779' / 'no original calibration equivalence claimed'. The 17,280 count parity is therefore count parity against a v2 envelope, not proof that the original F1779 calibration is reproduced. Count parity alone is not scientific acceptance.

gaps.title: F1849 premise corrected: F1779 Cases 3 and 5 used stress-error donors, not the damage envelope
gaps.detail: The handoff historical note and the report state that F1779 Cases 3 and 5 used stress-error donors, whereas this experiment constructs a damage-sizing envelope for all cases. All-damage sizing for Cases 3/5 is therefore a different experiment from F1779, not an F1779 reproduction. The F1849 task premise (reproduce all four F1779 meshes with the damage envelope) was partly incorrect. The handoff correctly identified this; it is recorded here as a finding, not as an execution defect.

findings.finding: Genuine mesh, visually inspected. Title states 17,280 elements, 97.25% quads, Gate 06 2.205x PASS, CONSTRUCTED_DAMAGE_ENVELOPE. The mesh shows a narrow dense band distal to the hole (x approx 0.75-1.0, y approx 0.6-0.7) and a dense patch at the notch-to-hole ligament (x approx 0.5-0.6, y approx 0.5); the rest of the plate is coarse. This is the tight damage-envelope pattern, distinct from the broad F1812 Case 2 (41,438 el). Count and visual pattern are consistent with the F1779 narrow-band description.

Genuine mesh, visually inspected. Title states 4,375 elements, 96.59% quads, Gate 06 1.338x FAIL, CONSTRUCTED_DAMAGE_ENVELOPE. The mesh is coarse overall: seven holes visible with only modest refinement around hole perimeters and inter-hole ligaments, no dense inter-hole band like F1779/F1812 Case 5 (15,330/15,466 el). The image visually confirms the negative result: the damage envelope on the elastic seven-hole donor produces an under-refined mesh (audit: 5.65% of elements at h <= l0, 0.02% at h <= l0/2). The FAIL is stated honestly in the title.
